        Taoist writings have been extensively catalogued and analysed by scholars, providing a wealth of material to assist followers in their understanding (pp. 1, 9 [1111]).

        1.10.3.4.2. Con:
        The Taoist canon suffers from a number of notable limitations and problems [1112].

    1.10.4. Con:
    Taoism is a source of human conflict.

      1.10.4.1. Con:
      Taoism teaches that the use of aggressive force is ineffective and unethical (p. 162 [1113]).

        1.10.4.1.1. Pro:
        Aggression often leads to a cycle that harms all the involved parties (pp. 25–26 [1114]).

        1.10.4.1.2. Con:
        Taoism is opposed to open aggression, but its principles support the use of hidden aggression and subterfuge [1115].

      1.10.4.2. Pro:
      Taoist teachers and authorities have contributed to anti-Buddhist propaganda [1116] and sentiment.

        1.10.4.2.1. Pro:
        The Taoist emperor Wuzong of Tang actively persecuted Buddhists [1117] and destroyed their monasteries.

        1.10.4.2.2. Con:
        The historical relationship between Taoism and Buddhism has primarily been one of support and mutual influence [1118].

      1.10.4.3. Con:
      Many Taoist principles, such as the use of non-action, are helpful in resolving modern conflicts (pp. 168–169 [1119]).

        1.10.4.3.1. Pro:
        Research has shown that Taoist principles can be usefully integrated into organisational conflict management (p. 5 [1120]).

        1.10.4.3.2. Con:
        The Taoist perspective on good and evil as projections of personal desires and fears [1121], while helpful in everyday conflict, is not especially useful with regard to moral evil [1122].

      1.10.4.4. Pro:
      Taoist dialectics have directly contributed to the development of Chinese military strategy [1123].

        1.10.4.4.1. Pro:
        Taoism has provided leaders with a moral justification for military action (p. 1 [1124]).

        1.10.4.4.2. Con:
        Taoism considers violence [1125] to be a last resort, and promotes other means of conflict resolution.

    1.10.5. Con:
    Taoism takes advantage of its followers.

      1.10.5.1. Pro:
      Many Taoist temples are heavily commodified [1126] and have been associated with exploitative development practices.

        1.10.5.1.1. Con:
        The commercialisation of Taoist religious sites [1127] has allowed the religion to expand after being nearly eradicated during the Communist takeover of China.

        1.10.5.1.2. Pro:
        A Taoist temple in Henan, China was closed by authorities when it was found to be generating profit despite its non-profit charter [1128].

      1.10.5.2. Con:
      Taoism has historically promoted altruistic behaviour and the nurturing of others (p. 22 [1129]).

        1.10.5.2.1. Pro:
        Selflessness and altruism are central elements in the foundational texts of Taoism (p. 15 [1130]).

        1.10.5.2.2. Con:
        Taoism does not support altruism in an absolute sense, but rather teaches that altruism and selfishness [1131] are two opposing forces that should be balanced.

      1.10.5.3. Con:
      Taoist temples have often acted as shelters for travellers, providing them with free lodgings and food [1132].

        1.10.5.3.1. Pro:
        Taoist temples in China offered refuge [1133] to those fleeing the 13th-century Mongol invasion.

        1.10.5.3.2. Con:
        Many Taoists oppose the promotion of tourism and temple visits [1134], preferring to focus on solitary ascetic practice.

      1.10.5.4. Pro:
      Taoism exploits its followers [1135] by teaching them that it is possible to attain physical immortality (p. 1 [1136]).

        1.10.5.4.1. Pro:
        The emperor Qin Shi Huang spent a great deal of his life and wealth pursuing Taoist elixirs that promised immortality [1137].

        1.10.5.4.2. Con:
        Although early Taoism was concerned with the development of physical immortality, this practice gave way to a focus on spiritual immortality and transformation [1138].

    1.10.6. Con:
    There is no evidence to support the assertions of Taoism.

      1.10.6.1. Pro:
      The concept of Tao [1139] is unfalsifiable [1140].

        1.10.6.1.1. Pro:
        Taoism expressly claims that Tao [1141] cannot be quantified or qualified in human terms.

        1.10.6.1.2. Pro:
        Taoism asserts that Tao gives rise to all things [1142], yet makes no empirical claim as to how this occurs.

        1.10.6.1.3. Con:
        Tao is a supernatural concept, and therefore need not be falsifiable through natural means.

      1.10.6.2. Pro:
      Taoism promotes superstitious practices.

        1.10.6.2.1. Pro:
        Taoism has absorbed a number of supernatural beliefs and practices [1143] from folk religion.

          1.10.6.2.1.1. Pro:
          Taoism has supported the use of the I Ching [1144] for divination [1145] purposes.

        1.10.6.2.2. Con:
        A lack of cultural understanding has fueled misperceptions [1146] of Taoist rituals as superstition.

        1.10.6.2.3. Pro:
        Taoists engage in pseudoscientific practices, such as Feng Shui [1147] and TCM [1148].

          1.10.6.2.3.1. Con:
          Both Feng Shui and TCM make use of the placebo effect, so they can still have beneficial [1149] effects.

      1.10.6.3. Con:
      Taoism is closely associated with the development of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) via scientific experimentation [1150].

        1.10.6.3.1. Pro:
        There is a great deal of clinical and experimental evidence [1151] of the efficacy of TCM in Chinese-language sources.

        1.10.6.3.2. Con:
        The evidence supporting the use of herbal medicines in TCM often suffers from methodological weaknesses (p. 211 [1152]).

      1.10.6.4. Con:
      There is very little in Taoist cosmology and creation that contradicts accepted science [1153].

        1.10.6.4.1. Con:
        The Taoist creation narrative [1154] contradicts the scientific evidence of Earth's formation [1155] and the development of humanity [1156].

        1.10.6.4.2. Pro:
        The ambiguous nature of Tao can encompass scientific and atheistic beliefs.

  1.11. Thesis:
  Hinduism [1157]

    1.11.1. Pro:
    Following Hinduism has positive benefits for the individual.

      1.11.1.1. Pro:
      Hinduism is the foundation for yoga, meditation, pranayama, and ayurveda – all of which have been found to improve physical and mental health [1158].

        1.11.1.1.1. Pro:
        Some studies have found that Hindus have the highest life satisfaction rate [1159] of any religious or non-religious group.

          1.11.1.1.1.1. Pro:
          Hinduism promotes a reliance on intrinsic rather than extrinsic [1160] sources of happiness, which is associated with increased well-being (p. 197 [1161]).

          1.11.1.1.1.2. Con:
          Religiosity in general has been demonstrated to improve overall life satisfaction (p. 8 [1162]); Hinduism is not exceptional in this regard.

        1.11.1.1.2. Con:
        One can practise yoga [1163], meditation [1164], ayurveda [1165], or pranayama [1166] without following Hinduism.

          1.11.1.1.2.1. Pro:
          Yoga has become increasingly popular, with over 300 million people [1167] around the world participating in some form of yoga practice.

          1.11.1.1.2.2. Con:
          Some yoga and pranayama techniques can be dangerous if performed improperly [1168]; it is better to find a guru from an established Hindu tradition.

        1.11.1.1.3. Pro:
        The ayurvedic diet [1169] followed by many Hindus is widely considered to promote health and well-being.

          1.11.1.1.3.1. Pro:
          The ayurvedic diet has been shown to promote weight loss, improve digestion [1170], and reduce the symptoms of many gastrointestinal conditions.

          1.11.1.1.3.2. Con:
          Ayurvedic diets can be confusing for beginners [1171] and can feel restrictive to those accustomed to a broader range of foods.

      1.11.1.2. Pro:
      The rituals and traditions of Hinduism contribute to the development of personal identity and a sense of community belonging (pp. 42–43 [1172]).

        1.11.1.2.1. Pro:
        Participation in Hindu festivals and collective actions promotes a sense of interconnectedness and well-being (pp. 97–98 [1173]).

        1.11.1.2.2. Con:
        The monistic foundations of Hinduism do not provide a sound philosophical basis for individuation and the development of selfhood (pp. 11–13 [1174]).

      1.11.1.3. Con:
      Mental health issues [1175] are stigmatised by Hinduism, which can make it difficult for followers to seek effective help.

        1.11.1.3.1. Pro:
        Hindus who acknowledge that they suffer from mental health issues face reduced marriage prospects and social shunning (pp. 364, 367 [1176]).

        1.11.1.3.2. Con:
        Hinduism teaches that every illness has a biological, psychological, and spiritual element; this offers those suffering from mental illness an opportunity to learn more about the way their mind works and find meaning (pp. 5–6 [1177]).

      1.11.1.4. Con:
      Hinduism teaches adherents to follow satgurus [1178], or enlightened masters, who often make claims about their followers' spiritual states based upon purported arcane knowledge and powers.

        1.11.1.4.1. Pro:
        Anyone can claim to be a guru, as there are no necessary qualifications. [1179]

        1.11.1.4.2. Con:
        Gurus can be of great benefit to their students, providing insight, guidance, and inspiration [1180] to help them on their spiritual journeys.

    1.11.2. Pro:
    Hinduism is a complete and well-established system of belief.

      1.11.2.1. Con:
      Hinduism lacks a central organisational structure [1181].

        1.11.2.1.1. Pro:
        Hinduism is a modern attempt to present a wide range of different ethnocultural beliefs [1182] as an organised religion; in practice, Hinduism is highly decentralised [1183].

        1.11.2.1.2. Con:
        The absence of a central institution allows Hindu priests to be selected and judged on the quality of their work [1184] in the community rather than their relationship with a larger organisation.

      1.11.2.2. Pro:
      Hinduism has played a central role in the development of Indian and Southeast Asian society.

        1.11.2.2.1. Con:
        Hinduism contributed to the Indian colonisation of Southeast Asia [1185].

          1.11.2.2.1.1. Con:
          The Indian influence on Southeast Asia was predominantly an exchange of ideas [1186] rather than an example of territorial conquest.

          1.11.2.2.1.2. Pro:
          The Hindu caste system [1187] took hold in a number of Southeast Asian countries.

        1.11.2.2.2. Pro:
        Hinduism was instrumental in spreading more advanced literature, art, architecture, language, and philosophy [1188] throughout Asia.

          1.11.2.2.2.1. Pro:
          There are thousands of Hindu temples [1189] both within India and around the world [1190].

      1.11.2.3. Con:
      The important schools of Hindu thought are at odds with each other on important doctrines.

        1.11.2.3.1. Con:
        The diversity of Hindu philosophy enhances the richness of Hindu culture [1191].

        1.11.2.3.2. Pro:
        The Dvaita [1192], Advaita [1193], and Visishtadvaita [1194] schools of thought disagree on the basic nature of existence.

      1.11.2.4. Pro:
      Hinduism comprises many distinct traditions and beliefs with thousands of years of rich history.

        1.11.2.4.1. Con:
        The vast number of Hindu gods and practices [1195] can be overwhelming and confusing for adherents.

        1.11.2.4.2. Pro:
        Hindu philosoph [1196]y has been extensively developed [1197] in thousands of works [1198] that elaborate, explain, and support [1199] its belief system.

          1.11.2.4.2.1. Con:
          The majority of Hindu practices are based on Smriti [1200] or Puranas [1201], colorful and illustrative contemporary commentaries, rather than Shruti [1202], the eternal truths realised by ancient sages.

    1.11.3. Pro:
    Following Hinduism is beneficial to society.

      1.11.3.1. Con:
      Hinduism promotes the social designations of a caste system [1203], which is nothing more than a means of oppressing a group of people [1204] based on the circumstances of their birth.

        1.11.3.1.1. Con:
        There is no prescription for a caste system in Hinduism. Unrelated concepts [1205] have been misinterpreted [1206] as prescriptions for a caste system [1207].

        1.11.3.1.2. Pro:
        Social, economic, and political systems co-evolve with religion, which is then used to justify them. Hinduism should be criticised insofar as it does little to challenge the caste system [1208].

      1.11.3.2. Pro:
      Some schools of Hinduism endorse a pantheistic worldview [1209], where one believes everything is God; this results in more compassion towards the universe.

        1.11.3.2.1. Pro:
        Certain schools of Hinduism espouse a non-dualistic philosophy [1210].

        1.11.3.2.2. Con:
        Many believe that pantheistic views inadequately address the existence of evil [1211].

      1.11.3.3. Pro:
      Hinduism promotes moral values that are beneficial to society (p. 286 [1212]).

        1.11.3.3.1. Pro:
        Many Hindu values are based upon a belief in the inherent worth of both human and non-human life [1213].

        1.11.3.3.2. Con:
        The Kama Sutra gives advice on how to commit adultery [1214].

          1.11.3.3.2.1. Con:
          According to the Supreme Court of India, prohibiting adultery is a violation of human freedom (p. 59 [1215]).

      1.11.3.4. Con:
      Hinduism is associated with misogyny and the abuse of women and girls [1216] (p. 1445 [1217]).

        1.11.3.4.1. Pro:
        Hinduism continues to support the practice of arranged marriage (p. 244 [1218]).

          1.11.3.4.1.1. Pro:
          Although illegal, child marriage [1219] among Hindus in India is widespread [1220].

        1.11.3.4.2. Con:
        Femininity is revered in Hinduism, and women and mothers are considered equal to men [1221].

    1.11.4. Con:
    Hinduism is a source of human conflict.

      1.11.4.1. Pro:
      Hinduism has contributed to ongoing strife both within India [1222] and between India and Pakistan [1223].

        1.11.4.1.1. Pro:
        Historical mistreatment of the Muslim majority in Kashmir by Hindu leaders contributed to to the split between India and Pakistan (p. 1 [1224]).

        1.11.4.1.2. Con:
        The strife between India and Pakistan is largely a result of British colonial policies and British withdrawal amidst the Indian Partition [1225].

      1.11.4.2. Con:
      Hinduism accepts other religions [1226] as valid and beneficial spiritual paths.

        1.11.4.2.1. Pro:
        Hinduism has no dogma; there are even atheist Hindus [1227].

        1.11.4.2.2. Pro:
        Hinduism asserts the truth of its teachings while admitting the possibility that other religions are equally true [1228].

        1.11.4.2.3. Con:
        If all religions are right, then there is no standard to measure truth other than by feelings and emotions.

          1.11.4.2.3.1. Con:
          There is a standard to measure truth. Pramanas [1229] are used by philosophical schools to measure truth.

      1.11.4.3. Pro:
      Hinduism has become entrenched in Indian politics, giving rise to exclusionary religious nationalist [1230] ideologies.

        1.11.4.3.1. Pro:
        Hindu Nationalism [1231] is associated with right-wing extremism and discrimination against Muslim minorities.

        1.11.4.3.2. Con:
        Indian nationalism is a political rather than religious movement [1232]; Hinduism should not be blamed for the actions of political leaders.

      1.11.4.4. Con:
      The values and teachings of Hinduism are conducive to conflict resolution [1233].

        1.11.4.4.1. Pro:
        Hinduism places a higher value on the moral consequences of actions than on truth in the absolute sense (p. 25 [1234]).

        1.11.4.4.2. Con:
        Hinduism condones the use of force [1235] when other attempts to avoid conflict have failed.

    1.11.5. Con:
    There is no evidence to support the assertions of Hinduism.

      1.11.5.1. Con:
      There is evidence of many Hindu miracles [1236].

        1.11.5.1.1. Pro:
        A Hindu sage was able to miraculously [1237] survive without water or food for over 15 days.

          1.11.5.1.1.1. Con:
          Other researchers have noted inconsistencies in the methodology of the study; for example, Jani was allowed to gargle and bathe [1238], which would have allowed him the opportunity to drink water.

            1.11.5.1.1.1.1. Pro:
            A number of other adherents have died [1239] whilst attempting such ordeals.

        1.11.5.1.2. Con:
        Many supposed miracles by Hindu mystics have been demonstrated to be spurious [1240] and intended to exploit public superstitions.

      1.11.5.2. Con:
      Many Hindus report being comfortable integrating scientific findings [1241] into their religious belief.

        1.11.5.2.1. Pro:
        Hindus do not perceive a conflict between their religious beliefs and science; for example, most Hindus accept the Theory of Evolution [1242].

        1.11.5.2.2. Con:
        Hindu scriptures contain scientific errors.

          1.11.5.2.2.1. Con:
          Textual errors can be corrected.

          1.11.5.2.2.2. Pro:
          The Atharva Veda says that a bull supports the Earth [1243] and heaven, but there is nothing that physically supports the Earth.

      1.11.5.3. Pro:
      Hinduism promotes superstitious beliefs.

        1.11.5.3.1. Pro:
        Hinduism supports belief in astrology [1244].

        1.11.5.3.2. Con:
        Many Hindu leaders and reformers have openly opposed superstitious beliefs [1245].

      1.11.5.4. Pro:
      There is no reason to believe that Hindu gurus [1246] are spiritually enlightened prophets.

        1.11.5.4.1. Pro:
        Hindu gurus often rely on unclear prophecies [1247] about future events, such as asserting that the god Vishnu will return to Earth as an avatar named Kalki [1248].

        1.11.5.4.2. Con:
        Hinduism does not support belief in prophets [1249], so such teachers fall outside the accepted tenets of the religion.

    1.11.6. Con:
    Hinduism takes advantage of its followers.

      1.11.6.1. Pro:
      Hindu beliefs perpetuate rape culture and victim blaming (pp. 1, 3 [1250]).

        1.11.6.1.1. Con:
        Many of the scriptural examples in claims that Hinduism supports rape culture have been cherry-picked and taken out of context [1251].

        1.11.6.1.2. Pro:
        Eleven men convicted of raping a pregnant 19-year-old woman and killing her family were released from prison [1252] on the grounds that, as upper-class Brahmins, they inherently have good values.

          1.11.6.1.2.1. Con:
          The Supreme Court of India ultimately overturned their release [1253] and revealed that the remission of their sentences had been fraudulently obtained.

          1.11.6.1.2.2. Pro:
          There have been numerous examples of sexual assault by Brahmins being excused [1254] or used to discredit victims [1255].

      1.11.6.2. Pro:
      Hinduism promotes the practice of tithing [1256] to ensure prosperity, which can constitute financial abuse [1257].

        1.11.6.2.1. Pro:
        There have been numerous instances of purported Hindu gurus [1258] swindling their followers.

        1.11.6.2.2. Con:
        Tithing and donations to Hindu institutions have supported disaster relief efforts and provided humanitarian aid to those in need (pp. 48–49 [1259]).

      1.11.6.3. Con:
      Hinduism has been instrumental in the development of modern humanitarian law [1260].

        1.11.6.3.1. Pro:
        The ancient Manusmriti established rules governing the proper treatment of enemy soldiers and non-combatants during wartime (p. 5 [1261]).

        1.11.6.3.2. Con:
        The Hindu caste system is inherently exploitative [1262] and opposed to humanitarian goals.

      1.11.6.4. Con:
      Hindu beliefs about dying and reincarnation can help followers dealing with anxiety about death [1263].

        1.11.6.4.1. Pro:
        Hindu beliefs about death have proven useful for therapists addressing the psychological effects of the coronavirus pandemic (pp. 4–5 [1264]).

        1.11.6.4.2. Con:
        Hinduism teaches that there are negative effects in the afterlife [1265] for those who break moral codes whilst living, and thereby it continues to support the fear of death.

  1.12. Thesis:
  Rastafarianism [1266]

    1.12.1. Pro:
    Following Rastafarianism is beneficial to society.

      1.12.1.1. Pro:
      Rastafarianism is opposed to human oppression (p. 28 [1267]).

        1.12.1.1.1. Pro:
        The practices and distinctive culture of Rastafarianism emerged as a reaction against the systemic oppression of African people [1268] in the Western world.

        1.12.1.1.2. Con:
        Rastafarianism poses a threat [1269] to the rights of the LGBTQ+ [1270] community.

      1.12.1.2. Con:
      Rastafarianism is opposed to contraception and abortion rights [1271].

        1.12.1.2.1. Pro:
        Rastafarianism considers contraception and abortion to be colonial strategies for limiting the population of African peoples (p. 14 [1272]).

        1.12.1.2.2. Con:
        Even if opposed to abortion for themselves, Rastafarians can still support the choices of others and provide medical help to women in need (p. 3 [1273]).

      1.12.1.3. Pro:
      Rastafarianism promotes a positive relationship with nature and supports beneficial environmental practices (p. 16 [1274]).

        1.12.1.3.1. Pro:
        Rastafarianism supports the use of sustainable farming practices [1275] and forbids the use of harmful GMOs and pesticides [1276].

        1.12.1.3.2. Con:
        In the absence of pesticides and fertilisers, most Rastafarian farmers rely heavily on slash and burn agriculture (p. 2 [1277]); such practices are associated with a number of environmental harms [1278].

      1.12.1.4. Con:
      Rastafarianism espouses misogynistic [1279] values and beliefs.

        1.12.1.4.1. Con:
        Some have argued that the misogynistic elements associated with Rastafarianism are related to Jamaican culture [1280] rather than religion.

        1.12.1.4.2. Pro:
        The Rastafarian amalgamation of different belief systems subjects women to a wide range of cultural and religious prohibitions and judgments [1281].

        1.12.1.4.3. Pro:
        In Rastafarian communities, women suffering from domestic violence are often shamed into remaining silent [1282].

    1.12.2. Pro:
    Rastafarianism is a complete and well-established system of belief.

      1.12.2.1. Con:
      Rastafarianism lacks a central organisational structure and doctrine [1283].

        1.12.2.1.1. Con:
        The bureaucratic structures [1284] often found in organised religions represent oppression [1285] to Rastafarians, so local and individual organisation is preferred.

        1.12.2.1.2. Pro:
        With its emphasis on the individual discernment of God's will [1286], Rastafarianism is more accurately described as a mystical [1287] movement than an organised religion.

      1.12.2.2. Pro:
      Individual sects of Rastafarianism have their own leadership and teachings [1288].

        1.12.2.2.1. Pro:
        The well-known sects of Rastafarianism have priests, spokespeople, and supporting officers [1289].

        1.12.2.2.2. Con:
        As Rastafarianism relies heavily on personal interpretations [1290], there is a great deal of disunity [1291] between different branches; such rifts have made it easier for governments to continue denying the rights of Rastafarian people.

      1.12.2.3. Con:
      Rastafarianism is an amalgamation of beliefs from Christianity [1292], Judaism [1293], and Pan-African sociopolitics [1294] rather than a distinct religion.

        1.12.2.3.1. Pro:
        Rastafarian belief relies on the Bible; its religious elements are essentially a radical reinterpretation of Christian scripture [1295].

        1.12.2.3.2. Con:
        The syncretic elements of Rastafarian belief do not detract from its authenticity as a distinct religion (pp. 86, 97 [1296]).

      1.12.2.4. Pro:
      Scholarly research has supported Rastafarian claims of legitimacy [1297] in the face of social and government suppression.

        1.12.2.4.1. Pro:
        A group of Catholic scholars concluded their study of Rastafarianism by upholding its legitimacy as a distinct religion [1298] and recommending that it be afforded equal respect to other faiths.

        1.12.2.4.2. Con:
        Many Rastas argue that Rastafarianism is not a religion [1299].

    1.12.3. Pro:
    Following Rastafarianism has positive benefits for the individual.

      1.12.3.1. Pro:
      Marijuana is considered a sacrament [1300] in Rastafarianism; smoking ganja facilitates Rastafarian contemplation and invokes spiritual meaning (p. 15 [1301]).

        1.12.3.1.1. Pro:
        Marijuana can help with pain management [1302] and so encouragement of its use by religious organisations may be highly beneficial.

        1.12.3.1.2. Con:
        Smoking marijuana can be addictive [1303], and may increase risk of stroke and heart disease [1304]; therefore, it is irresponsible for Rastafarianism to encourage consuming it.

      1.12.3.2. Pro:
      The dietary restrictions [1305] practised by Rastafarians promote good health [1306].

        1.12.3.2.1. Pro:
        The vegan Ital diet [1307] practised by Rastafarians places an emphasis on locally and responsibly sourced food [1308].

        1.12.3.2.2. Con:
        Despite a lack of evidence [1309], many Rastafarians believe that metal cookware is harmful [1310] to human health.

      1.12.3.3. Con:
      Rastafarianism is not equally welcoming of all people; a focus on the downpression [1311] of African people by Europeans makes the religion unwelcoming to white people.

        1.12.3.3.1. Pro:
        The founding principles of Rastafarianism, as laid out by Leonard P. Howell, are explicitly anti-white [1312].

        1.12.3.3.2. Con:
        Modern sects of Rastafarianism are open to people of any ethnicity who oppose the downpressing of African people [1313] and reject the corruption associated with Western culture.

      1.12.3.4. Con:
      The Rastafarian worldview glorifies suffering without offering realistic solutions to problems, such as poverty, unemployment, and violence (pp. 1, 26 [1314]).

        1.12.3.4.1. Con:
        Rastafarianism emerged during a period of intense oppression for Jamaican people, and many inequalities have continued through the present day, so it is understandable that suffering remains a key focus of the religion (p. 525 [1315]).

        1.12.3.4.2. Pro:
        Rastafarianism has diverted the energies of Jamaican people [1316] away from productive protest and social change.

    1.12.4. Con:
    Rastafarianism takes advantage of its followers.

      1.12.4.1. Pro:
      Rastafarianism opposes its practices and fashions being monetised [1317] in popular culture [1318] and tourism [1319] by followers, who may rely on such income.

        1.12.4.1.1. Pro:
        In response to the historical oppression of Rastafarians [1320], the Jamaican government has shifted to actively promoting Rasta culture as a way to drive tourism (p. 27 [1321]).

        1.12.4.1.2. Con:
        Although some Rastafarians have welcomed cultural tourism as a lucrative industry (p. 2 [1322]), many consider it a harmful manifestation of colonialism [1323] linked to other ills, such as sex tourism [1324].

      1.12.4.2. Pro:
      There have been allegations of child abuse [1325] by Rastafarian elders.

        1.12.4.2.1. Pro:
        The respect afforded to Rastafarian priests in their communities can easily be misused to gain access to child victims [1326] (p. 89 [1327]).

        1.12.4.2.2. Con:
        Rastafarianism lacks a central priesthood; as such, it is not associated with widespread institutionalised abuse (p. 6 [1328]).

      1.12.4.3. Con:
      Rastafarians often contribute to humanitarian efforts in their communities.

        1.12.4.3.1. Pro:
        The Rastafari Movement UK has helped provide ital food to poor Rasta families [1329] during the coronavirus pandemic.

        1.12.4.3.2. Con:
        Although Rastafarians consider Marcus Garvey a prophet [1330], he was found guilty of mail fraud for selling shares of a dubious shipping company that promised to help Jamaicans repatriate to Africa (p. 21 [1331]).

      1.12.4.4. Con:
      Rastafarian reasoning sessions help followers to integrate personal and objective knowledge in a way that supports personal identity (p. 98 [1332]).

        1.12.4.4.1. Pro:
        Rastafarian reasoning is distinctly opposed to cultural imperialism and helps followers develop an identity divorced from hegemonic cultural beliefs (pp. 14–15 [1333]).

        1.12.4.4.2. Con:
        The Rastafarian emphasis on cultivating African identity is reductive and overlooks many of the unique features of Afro-Caribbean culture and history (p. 8 [1334], p. 89 [1335]).

    1.12.5. Con:
    Rastafarianism is a source of human conflict.

      1.12.5.1. Pro:
      Rastafarians claim to be the direct descendants of the biblical Israelites [1336], which contradicts the history of the Jewish people.

        1.12.5.1.1. Pro:
        Some consider the Rastafarian identification with ancient Israel to be a case of cultural appropriation [1337].

        1.12.5.1.2. Con:
        Rastafarians should be free to identify with the Israelites if they so choose; such claims do not detract from Jewish history.

      1.12.5.2. Pro:
      Rastafarianism has continued to support the repatriation of Black people to Africa despite evidence that the policy is a failure [1338] (pp. 2–3, 5 [1339]).

        1.12.5.2.1. Pro:
        Many freed Black people, who had lived their entire lives in a different culture, had no desire to return to Africa (p. 2 [1340]).

        1.12.5.2.2. Con:
        The Shashemene land grant in Ethiopia is now home to over 130,000 refugees, many of whom are repatriated Rastafarians (pp. 157–158 [1341]).

      1.12.5.3. Con:
      Rastafarianism preaches peace [1342] and is opposed to violence [1343] apart from self-defence.

        1.12.5.3.1. Con:
        Rastafarians have participated in armed conflicts, such as the Grenada Revolution [1344].

        1.12.5.3.2. Pro:
        Despite efforts to debunk myths about Rastafarian criminality [1345], such beliefs have often been used as justification for widespread government harassment.

      1.12.5.4. Con:
      Rastafarianism has often been scapegoated [1346] for violence by police and other groups.

        1.12.5.4.1. Pro:
        The Jamaican government waited over 50 years to exonerate the Rastafarian community [1347] for eight deaths that occurred in 1963.

        1.12.5.4.2. Con:
        In 2001, a group of militant Rastafarians burned down a Catholic church in St. Lucia [1348], killing several parishioners.

    1.12.6. Con:
    There is no evidence to support the assertions of Rastafarianism.

      1.12.6.1. Pro:
      Rastafarianism is distrustful of scientific evidence, as it is seen as a tool of colonial oppression (p. 14 [1349]).

        1.12.6.1.1. Pro:
        Rastafarians are often opposed to modern medical interventions, such as vaccines (p. 14 [1350]).

        1.12.6.1.2. Con:
        From the Rastafarian perspective, such concerns are warranted. For example, the rapid expansion of the African slave trade was bolstered when colonial doctors identified the acquired resistance of African peoples to yellow fever and malaria [1351].

      1.12.6.2. Con:
      Rastafarian belief emphasises the value of personal experience over third-party evidence when evaluating the truth of a statement (p. 21 [1352]).

        1.12.6.2.1. Pro:
        The Rastafarian emphasis on personal experience acts as a bulwark against harmful indoctrination and racist ideology (pp. 6, 14 [1353]).

        1.12.6.2.2. Con:
        Anecdotal evidence [1354] is often a poor substitute for empirical facts as it has limited statistical significance and often triggers emotional judgments.

      1.12.6.3. Con:
      African people and cultures were systemically oppressed at the hands of Europeans via the transatlantic slave trade [1355].

        1.12.6.3.1. Con:
        Rastafarianism supports an Afrocentric [1356] view, which is associated with historical inaccuracies [1357].

        1.12.6.3.2. Pro:
        The frequent portrayal of Jesus as a white man, despite evidence to the contrary [1358], is a manifestation of the ongoing cultural oppression [1359] of people of colour.

      1.12.6.4. Pro:
      There is insufficient reason to believe that Haile Selassie I [1360] is God.

        1.12.6.4.1. Pro:
        Haile Selassie I is no longer alive [1361], and thus the claims of Rastafarianism that rely upon his divinity are substantially weakened.

          1.12.6.4.1.1. Pro:
          The remains of Selassie were discovered [1362] in 1992.

        1.12.6.4.2. Con:
        Haile Selassie I fulfilled biblical prophecies [1363].

          1.12.6.4.2.1. Con:
          Many rulers have been crowned with a title meaning 'King of Kings [1364]', including previous emperors of Ethiopia [1365].

          1.12.6.4.2.2. Pro:
          Selassie was crowned with the title 'King of Kings, Lord of Lords [1366]', which is a divine title [1367] in the Bible [1368].

        1.12.6.4.3. Pro:
        Selassie denied he was God [1369]. If he really was God, this would make God a liar.

        1.12.6.4.4. Con:
        Marcus Garvey's statement [1370] in 1920, 'Look to Africa, when a black king shall be crowned, for the day of deliverance is at hand', predicted the Messiahship [1371] of Selassie.

          1.12.6.4.4.1. Con:
          Garvey did not give a time limit on this prophecy; any black king crowned in Africa at any point in the future could be considered a fulfilment of it.

            1.12.6.4.4.1.1. Pro:
            Many other black kings existed in Africa around this time, such as King Ibrahim Njoya of Cameroon [1372]; there is no reason to assume this prophecy referred to Selassie.

  1.13. Thesis:
  Christianity [1373]

    1.13.1. Pro:
    Christianity is a complete and well-established system of belief.

      1.13.1.1. Con:
      Modern versions of the Bible are the product of numerous translations and interpretations [1374], which have undermined their authority.

        1.13.1.1.1. Pro:
        The various books of the Bible were written in several different ancient languages [1375] with widely differing intended audiences.

          1.13.1.1.1.1. Pro:
          The four synoptic gospels [1376] were written for different groups of people at different times long after the death of Jesus.

          1.13.1.1.1.2. Con:
          The canonical content of the Bible was determined by over 1,100 years of deliberation and debate [1377] amongst scholars and scriptural authorities.

        1.13.1.1.2. Con:
        The great number of biblical manuscripts [1378] still in existence make the Bible one of the most reliable ancient sources available in the world.

          1.13.1.1.2.1. Pro:
          There are approximately 25,000 manuscripts of the New Testament [1379]; over 5,600 in Greek and 10,000 in Latin.

          1.13.1.1.2.2. Con:
          The number and accuracy of manuscript copies are not evidence of the historical reliability of a source; for example, the different gospels contradict each other [1380] on a number of points.

      1.13.1.2. Pro:
      Christian belief is internally consistent and supported by biblical scripture.

        1.13.1.2.1. Pro:
        Despite the great number of denominations, all Christians share a common set of core beliefs and practices (p. 7 [1381]).

          1.13.1.2.1.1. Pro:
          Both Catholics and Protestants agree on the central tenets of the Christian faith (p. 1 [1382]).

          1.13.1.2.1.2. Con:
          Different Christian sects disagree on numerous significant doctrines and ethical matters [1383].

        1.13.1.2.2. Con:
        The Bible is subject to interpretation; many Christian authorities disagree on the correct interpretation of important passages.

          1.13.1.2.2.1. Con:
          Christianity has a long tradition of theological scholarship to support its assertions and interpretations (pp. 219–222 [1384]).

          1.13.1.2.2.2. Pro:
          Many Bible passages do not offer up a clear interpretation due to ambiguity or inconsistency [1385] in content [1386] or translation [1387].

      1.13.1.3. Pro:
      Established Christian organisations and institutions are ubiquitous throughout much of the world.

        1.13.1.3.1. Pro:
        There are over 45,000 different Christian denominations [1388] in existence, which demonstrates how its core doctrines can be adapted and localised [1389] for different groups.

          1.13.1.3.1.1. Pro:
          Christianity is the majority religion in 158 countries [1390]: two-thirds of all counties around the world.

          1.13.1.3.1.2. Con:
          The diversity of Christian denominations results in a great deal of infighting [1391] between different sects.

        1.13.1.3.2. Con:
        Only 19% of non-Christian religious people [1392] in the world personally know a Christian person.

          1.13.1.3.2.1. Pro:
          Christianity is not welcome in many parts of the world on account of its emphasis on evangelism [1393] and attitude of superiority.

          1.13.1.3.2.2. Con:
          The unfamiliarity of non-Christians with Christian people is a result of the association between religion and national identity [1394] rather than a result of Christian belief.

      1.13.1.4. Con:
      The Christian God's plan is incredibly convoluted and doesn't actually make much sense if we accept it as a viable representation of reality.

        1.13.1.4.1. Pro:
        The idea that human suffering is part of a benevolent God's plan is sadistic and incoherent [1395].

          1.13.1.4.1.1. Pro:
          God cannot be omniscient, omnipresent, omnipotent [1396], and omnibenevolent [1397] – as asserted by Christianity – since He fails to intervene on behalf of the innocent [1398].

          1.13.1.4.1.2. Con:
          Human suffering is a result of the improper use of free will; individuals suffer when they choose evil rather than good [1399].

        1.13.1.4.2. Con:
        Something being convoluted doesn't mean that it doesn't make sense. The wave-particle duality of light seems convoluted but still makes sense when studied and understood.

          1.13.1.4.2.1. Con:
          Unlike Christian belief, wave-particle duality [1400] can be empirically tested and validated.

          1.13.1.4.2.2. Pro:
          It is impossible for finite human beings to understand the plan of an infinite God [1401].

    1.13.2. Pro:
    Following Christianity has positive benefits for the individual.

      1.13.2.1. Pro:
      Christian rites are lavish, intense, and beautiful [1402]. This aesthetic enrichment [1403] improves life greatly.

        1.13.2.1.1. Pro:
        Grandiose architecture [1404], rich art, lavish altar decorations, incense, and colourful robes [1405] help establish a pious atmosphere.

          1.13.2.1.1.1. Pro:
          The aesthetics of Christian churches and shrines are conducive to the creation of liminal space [1406], wherein participants can experience transformation (p. 6 [1407]).

          1.13.2.1.1.2. Con:
          Luxurious churches and costly art and vestments are stark contrast to the modesty of Jesus's life and teachings [1408].

        1.13.2.1.2. Con:
        Given the ubiquitous focus on death, such as graphic imagery of Jesus's crucifixion [1409], many churches have a macabre atmosphere.

          1.13.2.1.2.1. Pro:
          The bread and wine consumed during Christian mass are believed by a number of sects to miraculously become the literal body and blood of Jesus [1410] and therefore constitute a form of ritualised cannibalism [1411].

          1.13.2.1.2.2. Con:
          Since the crucifixion of Jesus opened the path to his resurrection [1412], mankind's redemption [1413], and the fulfillment of God's plan [1414], the cross is also considered a joyful [1415] symbol by many Christians.

      1.13.2.2. Pro:
      Christianity provides followers with a sense of community [1416].

        1.13.2.2.1. Pro:
        The sense of community belonging fostered by Christian churches improves the overall life satisfaction of followers (p. 151 [1417]).

          1.13.2.2.1.1. Con:
          The key elements of community participation and resulting health benefits can be equally obtained through secular community participation (p. 1 [1418]).

          1.13.2.2.1.2. Pro:
          Christian churches offer a wide variety of events, conferences, retreats, courses, and live streams to promote participation [1419].

        1.13.2.2.2. Con:
        Some Christian denominations are taught to shun non- and ex-believers, which causes unnecessary pain and social isolation [1420].

          1.13.2.2.2.1. Pro:
          The practice of shunning is supported by several Bible passages [1421].

          1.13.2.2.2.2. Con:
          Shunning derives from a misinterpretation of the Bible [1422] and is directly opposed to the principles of Christianity [1423].

      1.13.2.3. Con:
      Christianity frequently describes humanity and the world as 'fallen [1424]', which implies that humans are inherently flawed. This is an unhealthy view that overlooks the human capacity for growth and self-actualisation [1425].

        1.13.2.3.1. Con:
        The death and resurrection of Jesus, central to the Christian doctrine of redemption [1426], offers valuable insight into the psychological process of individuation [1427], enabling greater self-actualisation.

          1.13.2.3.1.1. Con:
          The Christian concept of vicarious atonement [1428] is immoral [1429]; one's responsibilities cannot be scapegoated away.

        1.13.2.3.2. Pro:
        The concept of original sin is immoral [1430]. The idea that each person is born with someone else's sin and is damned by default is cruel and unjust.

          1.13.2.3.2.1. Pro:
          The doctrine of original sin asserts that children who have not reached the age of accountability [1431] are nevertheless subject to the eternal sin of humanity.

      1.13.2.4. Pro:
      The Bible teaches good means of decision-making [1432].

        1.13.2.4.1. Con:
        Relying on direction from God [1433] is not a rational basis for making decisions.

          1.13.2.4.1.1. Con:
          The principles and values of Christianity, conceived of as the living word of God [1434], offer a compass that can help guide decisions.

          1.13.2.4.1.2. Pro:
          Those who believe that they are communicating directly with God are often suffering from psychotic spectrum disorders (p. 1 [1435]).

        1.13.2.4.2. Pro:
        Numerous passages in the Bible support the cultivation of a broader perspective that transcends one's momentary desires [1436].

          1.13.2.4.2.1. Pro:
          The book of Proverbs offers a wealth of practical advice that promotes wise decision-making [1437] via consideration of the context and related factors.

          1.13.2.4.2.2. Con:
          Christianity promotes the belief that good behaviour will be rewarded in the afterlife [1438], which detracts from the desire and attainment of earthly goals.

      1.13.2.5. Con:
      Some branches of Christianity [1439] have been accused of being cults [1440]. As such, people should not be encouraged to join them.

        1.13.2.5.1. Con:
        Given their membership and age, [1441] most Christian denominations do not fit the definition [1442] of a cult.

          1.13.2.5.1.1. Con:
          Some branches of Christianity impose behavioural controls [1443] upon followers that far exceed biblical authority or reason.

          1.13.2.5.1.2. Pro:
          Some branches of Christianity that have been accused of cultic behaviour have widespread, established membership and are open to the public [1444].

        1.13.2.5.2. Pro:
        The process of leaving some Christian churches has been described as "grueling [1445]."

          1.13.2.5.2.1. Pro:
          Churches often exert significant social pressure [1446] over members; leaving them can be highly destabilising and lead to isolation from one's family or existing social circle.

          1.13.2.5.2.2. Con:
          The decision to leave a church is a serious consideration [1447] with grave implications [1448]; as such, it should not be approached lightly.

    1.13.3. Pro:
    Following Christianity is beneficial to society.

      1.13.3.1. Con:
      Many Christian teachings are damaging to women and gender minorities.

        1.13.3.1.1. Pro:
        Numerous Christian churches remain staunchly opposed to homosexuality [1449].

          1.13.3.1.1.1. Pro:
          A number of Christian churches and denominations continue to support harmful practices such as gay conversion therapy [1450].

          1.13.3.1.1.2. Con:
          Some Christian denominations [1451] have an affirming position on LGBTQ+ issues.

        1.13.3.1.2. Con:
        The Bible teaches that God created men and women to be equal in value [1452].

          1.13.3.1.2.1. Pro:
          The Bible clearly asserts [1453] that both men and women are created in God's image and are equally worthy of redemption and God's love.

          1.13.3.1.2.2. Con:
          Several Christian sects [1454] teach the doctrine of specific gender roles [1455] that promote the subservience of women [1456] to men and the submission of wives to their husbands [1457].

            1.13.3.1.2.2.1. Pro:
            In some denominations, victims of domestic violence [1458] are expected to endure abusive spouses.

      1.13.3.2. Con:
      Many Christian denominations hold harmful beliefs about medicine [1459] and sexual health [1460].

        1.13.3.2.1. Pro:
        A number of Christian churches teach retrogressive perspectives on birth control and abortion [1461].

          1.13.3.2.1.1. Pro:
          Some Christian denominations teach [1462] that condom use is sinful, which contributes to high rates of HIV/AIDS in Africa and other developing regions [1463].

          1.13.3.2.1.2. Con:
          Many Christian denominations have relaxed their stance on birth control [1464] and abortion [1465] in line with a more modern perspective.

        1.13.3.2.2. Con:
        Christian teachings on abstinence outside of marriage promote healthy sexual relationships [1466] and help followers to avoid unwanted complications [1467].

          1.13.3.2.2.1. Pro:
          Abstinence remains the most effective method [1468] of avoiding unwanted pregnancy and STIs.

          1.13.3.2.2.2. Con:
          Abstinence-only sexual education harms women and girls and denies their human rights [1469] (p. 19 [1470]).

      1.13.3.3. Pro:
      Christianity promotes absolute love [1471] and equality regardless of race or faith [1472].

        1.13.3.3.1. Con:
        Certain branches of Christianity are antisemitic [1473].

          1.13.3.3.1.1. Pro:
          After WWII, Pope Pius XII refused to allow Jewish child refugees who had been baptised as Christians during the war to return to their parents (pp. 11, 21 [1474]).

          1.13.3.3.1.2. Pro:
          The Catholic church has a history of allying with antisemitic groups [1475] and issuing official [1476] and unofficial [1477] publications with antisemitic content.

          1.13.3.3.1.3. Con:
          Antisemitism, and any other form of bigotry or hate, is antithetical to the teachings of Christianity [1478].

        1.13.3.3.2. Con:
        Christian scripture explicitly condones [1479] the practice of slavery [1480].

          1.13.3.3.2.1. Pro:
          American slavery [1481] was overwhelmingly supported [1482] by invoking Christianity (p. 3 [1483]).

          1.13.3.3.2.2. Con:
          The Bible condemns [1484] slave traders.

        1.13.3.3.3. Pro:
        A Christian's motivations are based in love and kindness [1485].

          1.13.3.3.3.1. Pro:
          The life of Jesus provides Christians with an example of perfect, unselfish love and forgiveness [1486].

          1.13.3.3.3.2. Con:
          Christianity hypocritically preaches love and forgiveness whilst simultaneously offering numerous justifications for violence [1487].

      1.13.3.4. Pro:
      Christianity teaches a beneficial moral code [1488].

        1.13.3.4.1. Con:
        If the God of the Bible is accurately depicted in the text, it would be morally necessary to oppose such a being [1489].

          1.13.3.4.1.1. Pro:
          In the Bible, God kills innocent children [1490].

          1.13.3.4.1.2. Con:
          It is not possible to meaningfully oppose an omnipotent and omniscient God, so even if God were evil, it would not be a moral obligation to oppose Him.

        1.13.3.4.2. Pro:
        The Christian Bible has a minimalist code of conduct.

          1.13.3.4.2.1. Con:
          The Old Testament lists over 600 rules that the faithful should follow, many of which are harmful to follow [1491] or otherwise problematic.

          1.13.3.4.2.2. Pro:
          Jesus directed his followers to love God [1492] and one another [1493].

      1.13.3.5. Pro:
      Christians promote humanitarian causes and socio-political good.

        1.13.3.5.1. Pro:
        Christian churches and organisations are a major source of aid [1494] in natural disasters and other humanitarian efforts [1495].

          1.13.3.5.1.1. Pro:
          There are a significant number of Christian relief and development agencies [1496].

          1.13.3.5.1.2. Con:
          Many Christian organisations inappropriately proselytise whilst delivering humanitarian aid (p. 5 [1497]).

        1.13.3.5.2. Con:
        Conservative Christian political values are associated with the denial of rights to marginalised groups (pp. 10–11 [1498]).

          1.13.3.5.2.1. Pro:
          In the US, Christian nationalists actively work to suppress the rights of ethnic and gender minorities [1499].

          1.13.3.5.2.2. Con:
          The basic teachings of Christianity promote compassionate assistance [1500] to those who are marginalised or oppressed.

    1.13.4. Con:
    Christianity is a source of human conflict.

      1.13.4.1. Con:
      The Bible preaches messages of peace [1501], which form the foundation of Christian pacifism [1502].

        1.13.4.1.1. Con:
        The Bible also describes many atrocities committed by God and His adherents, e.g., Noah's Flood [1503], the Plagues of Egypt [1504], and the slaughter of the Canaanites [1505].

          1.13.4.1.1.1. Pro:
          The wrath of God [1506] is mentioned over 600 times in the Bible.

          1.13.4.1.1.2. Con:
          According to Christian doctrine, the coming of Jesus and his redemptive sacrifice represent a progressive revelation of God's merciful nature [1507].

        1.13.4.1.2. Pro:
        The teachings of Jesus and the New Testament authors promote peace and non-violence [1508].

          1.13.4.1.2.1. Con:
          The Bible paints a conflicting image of Jesus with respect to peace; Jesus advocates for peace [1509] on some occasions, while renouncing peace [1510] in others.

          1.13.4.1.2.2. Pro:
          A number of Christian denominations are strongly associated [1511] with pacifism [1512].

      1.13.4.2. Con:
      Christianity is often falsely used as the justification for violence; many Christian leaders condemn [1513] this.

        1.13.4.2.1. Con:
        Regardless of whether such behaviour is denounced by church leaders, Christian beliefs have been the motivation for numerous acts of terrorism [1514] and hate crimes.

          1.13.4.2.1.1. Pro:
          Christian terrorism is increasingly becoming a primary threat [1515] to US national security (pp. 20–21 [1516]).

          1.13.4.2.1.2. Con:
          The Bible expressly condemns the use of violence against innocents [1517] and other aspects of terrorism.

        1.13.4.2.2. Pro:
        Secular leaders have used Christianity as an excuse or justification for politically motivated wars (pp. 198–199 [1518]).

          1.13.4.2.2.1. Pro:
          Most wars are fought over territory, resources, or power [1519], and Christian beliefs have often acted as a deterrent to such conflicts.

          1.13.4.2.2.2. Con:
          If Christianity can be used as a motivation and justification for war, then it still serves to promote conflict (p. 18 [1520]).

      1.13.4.3. Pro:
      Christianity is exclusive and aggressive towards other religions.

        1.13.4.3.1. Pro:
        Christianity has been responsible for a number of religiously motivated wars, including the Crusades [1521], the Thirty Years' War [1522], and numerous wars and conflicts [1523] between different Christian denominations.

          1.13.4.3.1.1. Con:
          The Crusades were an act of self-defence against Muslim aggression and encroachment [1524] on Christian territories.

            1.13.4.3.1.1.1. Pro:
            Although forced conversion is forbidden [1525] by Islamic law, Muslims killed and enslaved numerous Christians who refused to convert [1526] to Islam.

            1.13.4.3.1.1.2. Con:
            Jerusalem came under Muslim control four centuries [1527] prior to the first Crusade.

          1.13.4.3.1.2. Pro:
          Many scriptural passages directly support conquest [1528] and colonialism [1529].

        1.13.4.3.2. Con:
        Most modern Christians embrace religious tolerance [1530] and respect the fact that others may hold different beliefs.

          1.13.4.3.2.1. Con:
          Although Christianity may be tolerant of people practising other faiths, it generally refuses to accept other religions [1531] as equally valid spiritual paths.

          1.13.4.3.2.2. Pro:
          The concept of a separation between church and state [1532], which is essential to the existence of religious tolerance, is a product of Christian society.

      1.13.4.4. Pro:
      Christianity is associated with violent and harmful inquisitions [1533] and witch hunts [1534], which have included the killing [1535] of alleged heretics [1536] and witches [1537] and the burning of allegedly heretical writings.

        1.13.4.4.1. Con:
        Some historians claim that the scope of the inquisitions have been greatly exaggerated [1538].

          1.13.4.4.1.1. Pro:
          The number of executions performed by church tribunals during the inquisitions may be significantly lower than believed [1539], and many of the executions and tortures were actually carried out by secular authorities.

          1.13.4.4.1.2. Con:
          Even if the number of deaths during the inquisitions has been inflated, the immoral use of torture [1540] is not befitting of any religious organisation, much less one that preaches love and forgiveness.

        1.13.4.4.2. Pro:
        Christian churches are responsible for the destruction of countless documents they considered to be heretical or pagan (p. 295 [1541]).

          1.13.4.4.2.1. Pro:
          A great many texts from antiquity were completely eradicated by Christian censorship (p. 1 [1542]).

          1.13.4.4.2.2. Con:
          Christian monasteries [1543] have played a pivotal role in the preservation of countless ancient texts.

    1.13.5. Con:
    Christianity takes advantage of its followers.

      1.13.5.1. Pro:
      Christianity makes unrealistic demands of its followers.

        1.13.5.1.1. Con:
        No one is forced to follow Christianity; people voluntarily choose to follow it and embrace its demands, however unrealistic they may seem to others.

          1.13.5.1.1.1. Con:
          Christianity teaches that there is no path to salvation [1544] except through Jesus; this coerces followers to accept unrealistic demands.

          1.13.5.1.1.2. Pro:
          Jesus clearly stated that following his example would not be easy [1545].

        1.13.5.1.2. Pro:
        Christian teachings encourage followers to be perfect [1546], which is an unreasonable and unattainable goal.

          1.13.5.1.2.1. Pro:
          Christian expectations of perfection often lead to feelings of shame or guilt (p. 7 [1547]).

          1.13.5.1.2.2. Con:
          The Christian concept of God is a merciful one [1548]; Christianity teaches that God holds realistic expectations about humanity and does not judge people harshly [1549] for their flaws.

            1.13.5.1.2.2.1. Con:
            It is not clear that a merciful God is morally superior to a severe one, as mercy can allow harmful behaviour to continue unchecked.

            1.13.5.1.2.2.2. Pro:
            Much of the Bible is focused on the human struggle to do what is right; such stories highlight God's mercy [1550].

      1.13.5.2. Pro:
      Historically, some Christian denominations have enabled widespread abuse [1551].

        1.13.5.2.1. Con:
        Individuals claiming to be Christian do not necessarily follow Christian doctrine; the responsibility for such instances lies with individuals [1552] rather than Christianity as a whole.

          1.13.5.2.1.1. Con:
          Leaders [1553] in the Catholic Church [1554] have overlooked and downplayed the extent of abuse and have systematically protected [1555], and in some cases promoted, many offenders.

          1.13.5.2.1.2. Pro:
          The Catholic Church has demonstrated an increased willingness [1556] to hold abusers and their enablers accountable [1557].

        1.13.5.2.2. Pro:
        Certain Christian denominations are heavily associated with enabling sexual abuse, especially that of children [1558].

          1.13.5.2.2.1. Pro:
          There have been a number of recent sex abuse scandals [1559] involving Catholic clergy.

          1.13.5.2.2.2. Con:
          Christianity cannot be blamed for the abuse of children, as Christian teaching strictly opposes [1560] such behaviour.

      1.13.5.3. Pro:
      A number of Christian denominations take financial advantage of their followers.

        1.13.5.3.1. Pro:
        Christianity encourages its followers to be content [1561] with poverty, while Christian churches amass incredible wealth [1562].

          1.13.5.3.1.1. Pro:
          A number of modern Christian churches [1563] encourage their followers to donate beyond their financial means [1564].

          1.13.5.3.1.2. Con:
          Rather than encouraging poverty, Christianity teaches followers to seek spiritual goals [1565] beyond the acquisition of material wealth.

        1.13.5.3.2. Con:
        The bulk of donations to Christian organisations are entirely voluntary (p. 2 [1566]).

          1.13.5.3.2.1. Con:
          A number of modern Christian denominations [1567] continue to practice tithing [1568].

          1.13.5.3.2.2. Pro:
          Jesus emphasised that donations should be only be made willingly and for altruistic purposes [1569].

      1.13.5.4. Con:
      Christian communities operate a wide range of effective support groups [1570] for followers dealing with difficult life events.

        1.13.5.4.1. Pro:
        Christian institutions play a crucial role in providing addiction recovery services (pp. 1736–1737 [1571]).

          1.13.5.4.1.1. Pro:
          Christianity has been instrumental in the development of addiction recovery programs, such as Alcoholics Anonymous [1572].

          1.13.5.4.1.2. Con:
          Religion is not always beneficial for those in addiction recovery, as it can often become a source of new addictive behaviours [1573].

        1.13.5.4.2. Pro:
        Christian groups exist to provide support for those dealing with a divorce [1574] or death of a spouse [1575].

          1.13.5.4.2.1. Pro:
          Non-denominational Christian bereavement groups like GriefShare [1576] have been successful in instituting a wide range of support, services, and events for those suffering from the loss of a loved one.

          1.13.5.4.2.2. Con:
          Christian support for those undergoing divorce can be counterproductive, as Christian beliefs about divorce are often a source of stigma and shame [1577].

        1.13.5.4.3. Con:
        Many support and outreach programs by Christian churches are forms of covert evangelism [1578], where the true motive is to gain followers rather than to support the individual.

          1.13.5.4.3.1. Pro:
          Covert evangelism unethically instrumentalises people as a means to an end instead of dignifying them (p. 167 [1579]).

          1.13.5.4.3.2. Con:
          Most Christian support groups are open about their religious affiliation and use existing spiritual beliefs as a source of resilience and growth (p. 35 [1580]).

    1.13.6. Con:
    There is no evidence to support the assertions of Christianity.

      1.13.6.1. Con:
      A wide range of traditional and modern sources, including eyewitness accounts and video recordings, have offered evidence of demonic possession [1581] as described by Christian teaching, which are unexplainable by science.

        1.13.6.1.1. Pro:
        Many people find the Christian rite of exorcism [1582] to be an effective method for dealing with demonic possession.

          1.13.6.1.1.1. Con:
          The increased modern focus on possession and exorcism is a political tactic [1583] by Christian authorities to assert dominance over their followers.

          1.13.6.1.1.2. Pro:
          Exorcism has become increasingly popular in Mexico [1584] as a method for addressing cartel violence and the cult of Santa Muerte.

        1.13.6.1.2. Con:
        Research indicates that demonic possession is a psychopathlogical condition heavily associated with sexual shame and childhood abuse (pp. 92–93 [1585]).

          1.13.6.1.2.1. Pro:
          In many cases, exorcism can constitute abuse of mentally ill persons [1586] and, in certain cases, has resulted in their death.

          1.13.6.1.2.2. Con:
          An increasing number of exorcists have psychological training (p. 5 [1587]); many work with a team of psychologists and psychiatrists [1588] to rule out mental illness as the cause of a possession before proceeding with an exorcism.

            1.13.6.1.2.2.1. Con:
            Psychologists and psychiatrists who rely on supernatural explanations are at odds with the scientific foundations of their disciplines (p. 53 [1589]).

      1.13.6.2. Con:
      There are many Christian miracles that cannot be explained by science.

        1.13.6.2.1. Pro:
        The Tilma of Our Lady of Guadalupe [1590] is a miracle [1591], unexplainable by science, showing the Virgin Mary's intervention in history.

          1.13.6.2.1.1. Pro:
          The pupils of the image show a triple reflection called the Samson-Purkinje effect [1592]. This effect was completely unknown at the time of the image’s formation.

            1.13.6.2.1.1.1. Con:
            While many believe that the magnified eyes of the portrait show the reflection [1593] of those present in the room, they can only be interpreted as human figures with imagination (p. 253 [1594]).

          1.13.6.2.1.2. Con:
          The Tilma has never been examined using modern techniques [1595], but in 1985, forensic investigators concluded that it was certainly produced by human hands and noted inconsistencies both within the image and in the legend of its origin (pp. 253–254 [1596]).

        1.13.6.2.2. Pro:
        The Miracle of the Sun [1597] at Fatima is proof of intervention of the Virgin Mary in history.

          1.13.6.2.2.1. Con:
          It is likely that the Miracle of the Sun is explicable as a meteorological event [1598].

          1.13.6.2.2.2. Pro:
          The unexplainable [1599] phenomena [1600] at Fatima were witnessed by over 50,000 people [1601].

        1.13.6.2.3. Con:
        Just because something is not explained by science, that doesn't mean that any other explanation [1602] is therefore true.

          1.13.6.2.3.1. Pro:
          If we cannot explain a phenomenon, the only correct answer is to honestly admit we don't know. Positing a supernatural explanation in the absence of any other one is an argument from ignorance [1603].

          1.13.6.2.3.2. Con:
          Dismissing the possibility of miracles in the absence of other explanations is an argument from incredulity [1604].

        1.13.6.2.4. Con:
        Many things that were once unable to be explained by science can now be explained [1605]; such miracles may yet prove to be explainable without recourse to a supernatural explanation.

          1.13.6.2.4.1. Pro:
          Science can now explain the Christian phenomenon of stigmata [1606] as a natural occurrence rather than a miracle.

          1.13.6.2.4.2. Con:
          Even if a purported miracle can be explained by reference to natural processes [1607], this does not necessarily mean that such processes have occurred.

      1.13.6.3. Pro:
      Christianity is often at odds [1608] with empirical science [1609].

        1.13.6.3.1. Con:
        Some Christian denominations [1610] are willing to change their beliefs based on scientific evidence.

          1.13.6.3.1.1. Pro:
          Despite historical opposition, the Catholic Church ultimately reversed its position and accepted the heliocentric model [1611].

          1.13.6.3.1.2. Con:
          A number of the central beliefs of Christianity are unfalsifiable [1612] and, as such, cannot be considered consistent with scientific thinking [1613].

        1.13.6.3.2. Pro:
        All the matter and energy in the universe came into existence with the Big Bang, but the teachings of many Christian denominations [1614] deny this.

          1.13.6.3.2.1. Pro:
          According to the Bible, the universe was created in six literal days about 6,000 years ago [1615], which is contradicted by a vast amount of scientific evidence [1616].

          1.13.6.3.2.2. Con:
          Many Christians believe that God makes use of naturalistic processes, such as the Big Bang [1617], to create and act in the world.

        1.13.6.3.3. Pro:
        The literal interpretation of the Christian creation [1618] narrative [1619] is incompatible with the empirical evidence for the evolution of species (pp. 20–21 [1620]).

          1.13.6.3.3.1. Con:
          Many Christians find their faith to be compatible with evolutionary theory [1621] and reject a literal interpretation of the biblical creation narrative.

          1.13.6.3.3.2. Pro:
          Animals [1622] and humans [1623] were not all created at the same time.

      1.13.6.4. Pro:
      A number of events described in the Bible that have been strongly disconfirmed by external evidence.

        1.13.6.4.1. Pro:
        There is no evidence for the global flood [1624] described in the Bible.

          1.13.6.4.1.1. Pro:
          A great deal of geologic evidence [1625] contradicts the global flood hypothesis.

          1.13.6.4.1.2. Con:
          Given the limited awareness of early people regarding the natural world, the Old Testament account of Noah's flood could have been about a local flood [1626].

        1.13.6.4.2. Pro:
        The city of Jericho [1627] did not fall as the Bible describes.

          1.13.6.4.2.1. Pro:
          Jericho was destroyed 100–300 years prior [1628] to Joshua's supposed conquest and remained uninhabited at the time.

          1.13.6.4.2.2. Con:
          There is evidence that Jericho was destroyed in a fire [1629], which is consistent with the biblical account.

        1.13.6.4.3. Con:
        A number of biblical passages are better understood as fiction [1630], allegory [1631], or metaphor [1632] rather than literal truth, so their lack of conformity with evidence is not necessarily problematic.

          1.13.6.4.3.1. Pro:
          Christianity has a short history of strict or literal interpretation of scripture (p. 308 [1633]); many Christian denominations do not insist on biblical literalism [1634] or infallibility [1635].

          1.13.6.4.3.2. Con:
          There is no demarcation of any kind between historical and allegorical sections of the Bible. For example, the origin of man and other historical accounts in the Bible are presented as equally real and accurate.

  1.14. Thesis:
  Scientology [1636]

    1.14.1. Pro:
    Following Scientology has positive benefits for the individual.

      1.14.1.1. Pro:
      Scientology provides individuals with tools for rational decision-making [1637].

        1.14.1.1.1. Con:
        Scientology promotes a lack of rational inquiry [1638].

        1.14.1.1.2. Pro:
        Scientology practices aim to rid the analytical mind of painful experiences and memories [1639], enabling clearer thought.

      1.14.1.2. Con:
      Children in Scientology are not permitted to enjoy childhood like their peers, and instead are expected to act as 'adults in small bodies [1640]'.

        1.14.1.2.1. Pro:
        Children's brains [1641] are impressionable and malleable: not allowing them the opportunity to 'be a child' harms their emotional and cognitive development [1642].

        1.14.1.2.2. Con:
        Treating children like adults allows them to feel respected [1643] and gives them a head start on learning important [1644] life lessons and concepts.

      1.14.1.3. Con:
      Scientology has often been accused of employing brainwashing [1645] techniques on followers.

        1.14.1.3.1. Pro:
        Researchers have identified numerous elements of brainwashing [1646] in Scientology's rehabilitation camps and programs, which can have profoundly negative psychological effects.

        1.14.1.3.2. Con:
        Scientology is opposed to any practice that reduces one's ability to think for oneself, including brainwashing and mind-control [1647], as this is contrary to its stated goals.

      1.14.1.4. Pro:
      Scientology teaches that psychiatry has consistently mistreated [1648] those with mental disorders and offers alternatives.

        1.14.1.4.1. Con:
        Scientology discourages people from reaching out to get the mental health aid [1649] they need and instead manipulates them with far-fetched ideology and pseudo-science (p. 17 [1650]).

        1.14.1.4.2. Pro:
        Some of the psychiatric treatments that Scientology opposes have had detrimental effects on patients and have been found to be disproportionately [1651] used on women and vulnerable individuals.

    1.14.2. Pro:
    Scientology is a complete and well-established system of belief.

      1.14.2.1. Pro:
      Some of the most famous and influential people [1652] in the world are Scientologists.

        1.14.2.1.1. Pro:
        The number of successful people in Scientology [1653] is indicative of the effectiveness of its teachings.

        1.14.2.1.2. Con:
        Scientology has developed programs specifically intended to draw in celebrities and cater to their unreasonable whims [1654] in order to boost its public image.

      1.14.2.2. Con:
      Scientology is founded upon writings that are best described as science fiction (p. 90 [1655]).

        1.14.2.2.1. Pro:
        The Xenu [1656] story of Scientology posits that Earth was an intergalactic prison planet where criminals were executed en masse, allowing the remnants of their souls to possess modern humans.

        1.14.2.2.2. Con:
        Scientology is primarily based on Hubbard's book 'Dianetics [1657]', which elucidates the religion's theory of mind and techniques for self-improvement. Other elements are later elaborations [1658].

      1.14.2.3. Pro:
      Scientology is a worldwide [1659] organisation, with churches and leaders in most major cities.

        1.14.2.3.1. Con:
        Some scholars consider the influence of Scientology to be on the decline, and several countries have classified it as a harmful cult [1660].

        1.14.2.3.2. Pro:
        The number of Scientology locations and holdings [1661] has increased dramatically since 2004.

      1.14.2.4. Con:
      The founder of Scientology, L. Ron Hubbard [1662], was not an ethical or trustworthy [1663] person.

        1.14.2.4.1. Con:
        L. Ron Hubbard received numerous awards for his contributions to humanitarian causes [1664].

        1.14.2.4.2. Pro:
        L. Ron Hubbard was a bigamist [1665], and he absconded to Cuba with his daughter, against her mother's wishes [1666], despite being unable to care for her.

    1.14.3. Pro:
    Following Scientology is beneficial to society.

      1.14.3.1. Pro:
      Scientology is open to all ethnicities and nationalities [1667].

        1.14.3.1.1. Con:
        The high cost of joining Scientology [1668] places it outside the reach of many unless they are willing to work for the church at exploitative rates.

        1.14.3.1.2. Pro:
        Scientology maintains an Office of Ethnic and Cultural Affairs [1669] to address instances of discrimination and other issues affecting minority groups.

      1.14.3.2. Pro:
      Scientology supports the equality of different sexes and genders [1670].

        1.14.3.2.1. Con:
        Some former Scientologists have claimed that the church is opposed to homosexuality [1671].

          1.14.3.2.1.1. Pro:
          Hubbard's book 'Dianetics [1672]', which forms the foundation of Scientology, refers to homosexuals as 'sexual perverts' (p. 8 [1673]).

          1.14.3.2.1.2. Con:
          Scientology has officially denied such allegations [1674], and a number of gay Scientologists [1675] have defended the church's stance on homosexuality.

        1.14.3.2.2. Pro:
        Scientology supports women's right to choose birth control and abortion [1676].

        1.14.3.2.3. Con:
        Hubbard expressly argued that women should not be allowed to take an equal part [1677] in politics and business.

      1.14.3.3. Con:
      Scientology has been called a 'cult of greed', and has been associated with a wide range of financial scams [1678].

        1.14.3.3.1. Pro:
        Hubbard is believed to have absconded with up to US$200 million in church funds [1679].

        1.14.3.3.2. Con:
        Scientology operates a disaster response program, which has provided assistance to those impacted by natural disasters and other tragedies (p. 2 [1680]).

      1.14.3.4. Con:
      Scientology does not support rational discourse and often responds to criticism with invective [1681].

        1.14.3.4.1. Pro:
        Rather than welcoming discussion and debate, Hubbard supported the idea that any investigation of Scientology should be treated as an attack [1682].

        1.14.3.4.2. Con:
        Scientology has been victimised by industries and organisations at odds with its goal of promoting independent thought, such as the pharmaceutical industry [1683].

    1.14.4. Con:
    There is no evidence to support the assertions of Scientology.

      1.14.4.1. Con:
      Scientology uses technology – such as the E-Meter [1684] – to evaluate and help improve the spiritual awareness of followers.

        1.14.4.1.1. Con:
        The E-Meters [1685] used by Scientology only measure the electric resistance of the user.

        1.14.4.1.2. Pro:
        E-Meters help Scientology auditors to identify harmful thought patterns [1686], thereby improving the spiritual awareness of adherents.

      1.14.4.2. Con:
      Scientology is based upon scientific research [1687], and can be empirically validated.

        1.14.4.2.1. Con:
        There is no evidence that thetans and engrams [1688] exist.

        1.14.4.2.2. Pro:
        L. Ron Hubbard claimed that the records of the extensive scientific investigation of Scientology methods were seized in a raid on his office [1689].

      1.14.4.3. Pro:
      L. Ron Hubbard's theories about the structure and function of the human mind were summarily rejected by the American scientific community for a lack of evidence [1690].

        1.14.4.3.1. Pro:
        Scientology often rejects [1691] modern scientific and medical progress and methodology.

        1.14.4.3.2. Con:
        There are a number of conflicting scientific theories about the structure of the human mind that continue to be debated and investigated by scholars (p. 526 [1692]).

      1.14.4.4. Pro:
      The creation account [1693] of the Church of Scientology is implausible.

        1.14.4.4.1. Pro:
        No support or evidence has been provided to support the assertion that Earth was a galactic prison planet [1694].

        1.14.4.4.2. Con:
        Like many creation myths, the Scientology narrative is often interpreted as allegory [1695] rather than fact.

    1.14.5. Con:
    Scientology is a source of human conflict.

      1.14.5.1. Pro:
      Scientology supports a policy of reprisal, known as Fair Game [1696], against those who are opposed to or leave the church.

        1.14.5.1.1. Pro:
        Scientology encourages its followers to completely disconnect [1697] from anyone who leaves the church.

        1.14.5.1.2. Pro:
        A number of people who have attempted to leave Scientology have alleged that they were threatened or harassed [1698].

        1.14.5.1.3. Con:
        The original Fair Game policy [1699] referred only to an individual's rights as a Scientologist and was rescinded by Hubbard himself in 1968.

      1.14.5.2. Pro:
      A number of Scientologists in the 1970s were found guilty of attempting to infiltrate the US government [1700] to steal documents and evidence about the church.

        1.14.5.2.1. Con:
        The Church of Scientology maintains that it acted legally and with good reason [1701].

        1.14.5.2.2. Pro:
        Scientology's 'Operation Snow White [1702]' aimed to infiltrate the US government and remove documents proving that the Church's leaders were benefitting commercially from its tax exempt status.

      1.14.5.3. Con:
      Scientology promotes freedom of religious belief and practice [1703].

        1.14.5.3.1. Pro:
        Scientology promotes interfaith dialogue and celebrates diversity [1704].

        1.14.5.3.2. Con:
        Although Scientology outwardly professes support for freedom of religion, adherents are expected to devote themselves solely [1705] to the religion to the exclusion of other belief systems.

      1.14.5.4. Con:
      Scientology actively encourages conflict resolution.

        1.14.5.4.1. Pro:
        Scientology offers teachings and has designed courses specifically on conflict resolution [1706].

        1.14.5.4.2. Con:
        Scientology's 'Third Party Law [1707]', which teaches that human conflict can never occur between only two parties, is patently false and encourages scapegoating.

    1.14.6. Con:
    Scientology takes advantage of its followers.

      1.14.6.1. Pro:
      Hubbard admitted that he created Scientology to make money from religion [1708].

        1.14.6.1.1. Pro:
        High-level Scientology services can cost over $1000 per hour [1709].

        1.14.6.1.2. Con:
